newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-QUEENSLAND END SUPER 12 LOSING STREAK.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-QUEENSLAND END SUPER 12 LOSING STREAK.

text.p: Queensland recorded their first win of the Super 12 season with an unconvincing 37-24 victory against Otago Highlanders on Saturday to end a five-match losing streak.
Queensland took a maximum five competition points by scoring four tries in their most prolific attacking display of a disappointing season to date.
The extra bonus point lifted them alongside Otago on six points at the bottom of the Super 12 table.
Despite the victory, Queensland did little to suggest they are capable of recapturing the form that carried them to the Super 12 semifinals last season.
The match, played at great pace but littered with errors from both sides, failed to excite a subdued crowd of 15,000 at Ballymore.
Queensland faded badly in the second half after scoring all their tries in the first half to lead 31-10 at the interval.
Australia test second rower John Eales added two penalties after half-time to keep the New Zealanders at bay late in the game.
"We played very well in the first half but let it go in the second half -- but the win is going to give us a lot of confidence. We're very relieved." Queensland fullback Tim Horan said later.
Queensland flyhalf Elton Flatley made an immediate impact on his return after two months on the sidelines with a broken rib by scoring his side's first try in the second minute.
Second rower Matthew Cockbain and winger Ben Tune stretched the home side's lead with further tries in a bright opening.
Otago winger Jeff Wilson narrowed the gap when he capitalised on a mistake by Flatley to score near the posts.
But Queensland centre Jason Little restored Queensland's advantage by finishing off a fine move after Horan gained possession near his own try line.
Eales converted all four tries and also landed three out of his four penalty attempts in an accurate display of kicking.

Otago gained some consolation by dominating for long periods in the second half. Their pressure was rewarded with a try by fullback Matthew Carrington and a penalty try after winger Manassa Bari was impeded by defenders as he tried to take a quick penalty tap near the Queensland try line.

Queensland flanker David Wilson endured a miserable match, suffering a recurrence of a shoulder injury in the dying minutes after being sent to the sin-bin for 10 minutes for an infringement in the ruck.

Queensland - Tim Horan (captain), Willie Carne, Daniel Herbert, Jason Little, Ben Tune, Elton Flatley, Brett Johnstone, Mark Connors, David Wilson, Toutai Kefu, Matt Cockbain, John Eales, Glen Panoho, Brendan Cannon, Dan Crowley.

Otago - Matthew Carrington, Jeff Wilson, Romi Ropati, John Leslie, Manassa Bari, Simon Culhane, Stu Forster, Isotolo Maka, Taine Randell (captain), Lio Falaniko, Steve Gordon, Simon Maling, Carl Hoeft, Anton Oliver, Kees Meeuws.
